entry.title: Add cron.sh: a cron-safe entry point for unattended runs
entry.content:
Add cron.sh: a cron-safe entry point for unattended runs

`run.sh` assumes an interactive shell. Driving it from cron directly gets
three things wrong, so wrap it:

- cron hands over a bare PATH, which omits ~/.local/bin and so hides the
  `claude` CLI the transcriber authenticates through.
- A transcription run can outlast a one-minute tick. flock -n skips the
  overlapping tick instead of queueing a second run against one ledger.
- `--max-images` bounds each tick, which also sidesteps the 50-image `--yes`
  confirmation that would otherwise stall a run with nobody there to answer.

Output goes to $HANDWRITTEN_STATE_DIR/cron.log, trimmed to the last 256K once
it passes 1M, so cron mails nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Prepare for open source: mermaid diagrams, source-image embed, licens…
entry.content:
Prepare for open source: mermaid diagrams, source-image embed, licensing, danki

Pipeline behavior:
- Transcribe hand-drawn diagrams as mermaid code blocks; freeform sketches
  fall back to > [!note] Diagram callouts. The source photo is now always
  embedded at the bottom of each note under a ## Source section, and the
  embed_source_image config flag is retired.
- Filename slug and note title now come from the body's leading # Heading
  when present, falling back to the Subject: label. No more double-H1 when
  the body already leads with a heading.

Repo prep for publishing:
- Add MIT LICENSE and SECURITY.md (local-only threat model, known caveats).
- Add danki.py: standalone URL/PDF/text -> Anki cards CLI, previously an
  ad-hoc script.
- Pin dependency versions in requirements.txt; document both reproducible
  and floating install paths in the README.
- Add docs/data-flow diagram (mermaid source plus PNG/SVG renders).
- Restructure the README to frame the repo as two tools (pipeline + danki).
